title: What's new in SCM: Subcontracting (2026 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Introduction and overview of subcontracting updates
How to install the Subcontracting extension
Component supply method in bill of materials
Subcontracting purchase order creation and structure
Work in progress items and transfer order creation
Basic warehouse location with put-away and serial number handling

features.name: Subcontracting extension
features.description: A new extension for Business Central that manages subcontracting operations including logistics of raw materials, work in progress items, and integration with warehouse handling processes.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are silently released it in minor update three, but in this time we did not pre-install it on new environments
caveats: silently released in minor update three without pre-installation
previously available on App Store but not forced

features.name: Component supply method
features.description: A new field in bill of materials lines that allows specifying how components will be supplied to the subcontractor: transfer from warehouse, consignment at vendor, or vendor supplied.
caveats: requires configuration in bill of materials before production order creation

features.name: Vendor location tracking
features.description: New field on vendor card to track components held at vendor location during subcontracting operations. Components remain owned by the company but are physically at vendor location.
caveats: applies only to consignment-at-vendor supply method

features.name: Warehouse integration for subcontracting
features.description: Subcontracting operations now benefit from the same powerful warehouse handling processes available for standard wholesale and manufacturing operations, eliminating need for different handling.

features.name: Subcontracting routing link and operations
features.description: Production routing lines can be marked as subcontracting operations with links to components. A new fact box shows subcontracting details and connected components for each routing line.

features.name: Create subcontracting order from routing
features.description: Ability to create a subcontracting purchase order directly from the production order routing line, without using the legacy subcontracting worksheet.
caveats: legacy subcontracting worksheet still available for bulk operations

features.name: Subcontracting purchase order structure
features.description: Purchase order created from subcontracting includes component lines, work operation lines, description lines, and instruction comment lines with automatic population from production order and routing.

features.name: Create production order info line setting
features.description: Manufacturing setup toggle that automatically inserts a comment line in subcontracting purchase order with the production order line description and finished good name.
caveats: controlled by toggle in manufacturing setup

features.name: Subcontracting component transfer lead time
features.description: Manufacturing setup field that specifies the lead time for transferring components to the subcontractor, used in planning calculations.
caveats: explained as being used in later demonstration

features.name: Subcontracting comments and instructions
features.description: Comment lines in subcontracting purchase order contain instructions for the subcontractor about what to do, including assembly instructions, inspection requirements, and attachment documentation references.

features.name: Line attachments for subcontracting instructions
features.description: Subcontracting purchase order lines can have attachments per line with instructions that flow from production routing. Toggles control whether attachments flow to production order and purchase order.
caveats: attachments are per-line and attached to purchase order line, not document header

features.name: Subcontracting details fact box
features.description: New fact box in purchase order showing connected production order, transfer orders, and production routing information for easy navigation.

features.name: Subcontracting comment in routing
features.description: Production routing lines have a subcontracting comment field that contains instructions for the subcontractor, inherited from standard tasks and copied to purchase order.

features.name: Work in progress item in routing
features.description: Routing operation can specify a work in progress item that represents a semi-finished state between raw materials and final product, transferred to subcontractor instead of raw materials.

features.name: Transfer order to subcontractor
features.description: Create transfer orders from main location to subcontractor location with separate lines for component transfer and work-in-progress item movement.

features.name: Work-in-progress ledger entries
features.description: Registers work-in-progress items in a new ledger entry type when transfer posting occurs, tracking WIP quantity at subcontractor and enabling calculation of return quantities.

features.name: Item charge assignment to purchase receipts
features.description: Allocate item charges from invoices to specific purchase receipt lines, including the ability to select production orders connected to receipts.
caveats: Requires purchase receipt to exist before allocation

features.name: Closest-match pricing for subcontracting
features.description: Subcontracting pricing uses closest quantity match rather than selecting the smallest price; system matches the order quantity to the nearest defined price bracket.
caveats: Different from standard purchase pricing logic

features.name: Minimum amount rule for subcontracting
features.description: Vendors can specify minimum order amounts per line; when order quantity is below minimum, the system divides minimum amount by quantity to calculate effective unit price.
caveats: May result in higher per-unit prices for small quantities

features.name: Warehouse receipt for subcontracting operations
features.description: When warehouse handling is enabled, create warehouse receipts instead of direct purchase receipts; supports item tracking assignment including serial numbers during receipt.
caveats: Only generates put-away if it is the last operation; otherwise registers production fact only

features.name: Inventory put-away for basic warehouse locations
features.description: For basic warehouse locations requiring put-away and pick (no warehouse receipts/shipments), create inventory put-away directly from subcontracting orders with support for serial number assignment.

features.name: Serial number assignment across multiple levels
features.description: Define serial numbers at production order level (copied to purchase order) or in purchase document itself (populated to inventory put-away); flexible definition point depending on process.

features.name: Multiple receiving methods for subcontracting
features.description: Subcontracting supports normal purchase document, warehouse receipt, or inventory put-away as receiving methods, with serial number support across all approaches.

quotes.text: we are silently released it in minor update three, but in this time we did not pre-install it on new environments
quotes.why_it_matters: Indicates the extension was released quietly without forcing adoption, gathered feedback, and is now being reintroduced at a different level

quotes.text: original subcontracting which was present in Business Central for many years was maybe a little bit limited
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that the new version significantly enhances legacy subcontracting capabilities with recently added components

quotes.text: subcontracting operations can benefit from the same warehouse uh processes. So, no need to handle them differently.
quotes.why_it_matters: Core value proposition - subcontracting now integrates with standard warehouse handling instead of requiring separate processes

quotes.text: As I mentioned, for new environments in the latest version, you will get up pre-installed.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that the app is now pre-installed on new environments, unlike in the earlier silent release.

quotes.text: Component supply method. So, what I'm trying to do here, I decided to use these three components in my subcontracting operation
quotes.why_it_matters: Introduces the key new field allowing three different component supply strategies for subcontracting

quotes.text: on vendor card, we have a new field where we will track components which are on vendor location. They still ours
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains new vendor card field for tracking consignment components physically at vendor but owned by company

quotes.text: Purchase order subcontracting purchase order is created and I can actually open it and check it
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates simplified workflow of creating subcontracting purchase order directly from routing instead of using legacy worksheet

quotes.text: create production order info line, which is on. And this one instruct system once subcontracting order is created to additionally insert comment line
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains manufacturing setup control that automatically includes production order context in subcontracting purchase orders

quotes.text: if subcontracting is like the second one, then we are probably giving to subcontractor not only raw materials. We're giving them something not finished.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies support for multi-stage subcontracting where work in progress items are transferred instead of raw materials

quotes.text: So, once I will post it, the first line will indeed create item ledger entries. The second one, no. No, it will be registered
quotes.why_it_matters: Introduces the work-in-progress ledger entry feature that tracks WIP quantities transferred to subcontractors.

quotes.text: In subcontracting we give closest match price. So, even if you are buying 200, it sounds you should not buy 200.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the fundamental difference between subcontracting pricing (closest match) versus standard purchase pricing (lowest price).

quotes.text: Because our vendor subcontractor wants minimum amount per deal. So, like whatever you order, not less than 100 per line.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the minimum amount rule that affects pricing calculation when orders are below the vendor's threshold.

quotes.text: So, system does it differently. If it's less than 100, put amount as 100 divided by quantity and this is your price.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the calculation logic for minimum amount rules: dividing minimum by quantity to derive effective unit price.

quotes.text: So, instead, what can I do? Create warehouse receipt, as expected.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that warehouse receipt is required when warehouse handling is enabled for subcontracting operations.

quotes.text: i can define it in the production order and then they will be copied to uh purchase order
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the flexible serial number assignment workflow across multiple document types in subcontracting processes.

quotes.text: You can use any receiving method you like, either normal purchase document, warehouse receipt, or inventory put away.
quotes.why_it_matters: Confirms that subcontracting supports multiple receiving approaches depending on warehouse configuration.
